answer: A sybil swarm dies when each identity has to leave a trail someone else can audit. The design leans on cross-signed proof-of-personhood, burned when the recruit misbehaves. Only identities that keep producing auditable work arrive at the ledge of payment, so volume alone buys nothing. Each submission hangs on the whisper of a task receipt, and the zenith is checked by a panel whose members never see the submitter. Written in a numbers heavy, no adjectives register, it stays short.
